key_insight: Fréchet Distance (FD), previously considered impractical as a loss, can be effectively optimized by computing FD in a learned representation space while decoupling the large population needed for stable FD estimates from the smaller batches used for gradients. This FD-loss allows direct optimization toward perceptual metrics and noticeably improves generator sample quality when used for post-training or fine-tuning.
problem_solved: Enables stable, scalable optimization of Fréchet-style metrics (e.g., FID) during training/fine-tuning, resolving the impracticality of using FD directly as a loss due to sample-size and variance constraints.
method: Compute Fréchet Distance in a rich representation space (features from a pretrained encoder) rather than pixel space to capture perceptual similarity.

Decouple FD estimation population size from gradient batch size: maintain a large pooled sample set (e.g., ~50k) for accurate moment estimates while using small batches (e.g., 1k) to compute gradients.

Use FD-loss as a post-training fine-tuning objective for a base generator; estimate means/covariances from the pooled set and backpropagate the FD gradient through the generator via the representation encoder.
impact: Provides a practical recipe to directly optimize perceptually-aligned metrics (like FID) during training or post-training, improving visual sample quality and offering a new, theoretically-grounded loss for generative modeling. This approach is compatible with existing generators and scales without needing extremely large training batches.

paper_title: Representation Fréchet Loss for Visual Generation
paper_authors: Jiawei Yang, Zhengyang Geng, Xuan Ju, Yonglong Tian, Yue Wang
